title: Maoz Tzur
description: The Hanukkah hymn sung after the candles are lit, to its old Ashkenazi tune, for 2 to 4 singers, in Hebrew (the words are shown in Latin letters). Verse 1 praises Hashem, the rock of my salvation, and asks for the Temple to be rebuilt; verse 5 tells the Hanukkah story: the Greeks defiled the oil, a miracle came from the one jar left, and the wise set eight days of song. Each verse sings its last line twice, as Idelsohn printed it.

credits.words: Hebrew piyyut signed Mordecai in its acrostic (13th century)
credits.tune: traditional Ashkenazi Hanukkah tune, from a 15th-century German folk song (printed by Baer after 1883 and Idelsohn 1911/12)
credits.arrangement: Stackapella, on A. Z. Idelsohn's harmony (1911/12)

licence.source: tune, words and harmony from A. Z. Idelsohn, Sefer ha-Shirim (Berlin: Hilfsverein der deutschen Juden, 5672, that is 1911/12), No. 83, "Ma'oz tzur", p. 77, headed "ne'ima mekubbelet" (an adopted tune, as his preface defines the term), in E major in common time, printed right to left in two to three voices with verses I and II under the notes and verses III to V below, kept here in E major; read from the scan at archive.org/details/32882013391126-seferhashirimko (leaf n88). The tune checked against Abraham Baer, Baal T'fillah oder Der practische Vorbeter (3rd edition, Frankfurt am Main, after 1883), No. 188, p. 58, in E major (archive.org/details/der-practische-vorbeter-baer; Baer died 1894), and The Jewish Encyclopedia, vol. 8 (New York: Funk and Wagnalls, 1904), p. 316, article "Ma'oz Zur" by Cyrus Adler and Francis L. Cohen (Cohen died 1934), which sets verse 5 in F major and names the acrostic Mordecai and the tune's source in a German folk song sung by German Jews by about 1450. Verses 1 and 5 (the Hanukkah verse), each with the printed repeat of its last line; the Hebrew transliterated in modern Israeli pronunciation
